∴ (3) is correct.

Infra-red thermometer
Objects at different temperatures emit different amounts of radiations. For example, a hot object emits more infra-red radiation than a cold object. Hence, the temperature of an object can be found out by measuring the amount of infra-red radiation it emits.
No contact between an object and an infra-red thermometer is required in measuring temperature. Therefore, infra-red thermometers are also called non-contact thermometers. 
Since non-contact thermometers do not touch the objects when they measure temperature, they do not change the temperature of the objects. Also, they can respond rapidly to the temperature change of the objects. 
(Reference: http://www.temperatures.com/rts.html)
